text:
anya: Quick heads-up — bringing up Noctua7B (llama-style arch) on the bench and seeing a token-stitch gap when we convert vocab+rotary. Short repro attached below. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

devon: saw similar once with hybrid headwraps — can you paste the conversion cmd and a tiny example?

anya: sure. conversion command we used:
```
python convert.py --from=llama --to=redwood --vocab-map=tokmap.json --rotary-mode=headwrap
```
failing sample: input "The cat sat on the" -> generation jumps with odd token in middle, logits spike at token id ~1423 then normalizes.

sam: can you dump token ids for that prefix? suspect tokenizer normalization + unk merging.

anya: token ids: [43, 129, 78, 9, 1423] — 1423 maps to a subtoken that should have been split into [1423, 2] per the old map. converter merged them.

maria: that smells like a vocab merge edge + rotary phase shift. When subtokens are merged the rotary sin/cos indexing for heads can misalign by head_size multiples.

devon: ugh. that would also break kv-cache indexing (k/v offsets assume stable token segmentation). Can you repro with kvcache warmup?

anya: yes, with kvcache enabled the subsequent tokens' attention drifts after the merged token. ran a quick trace:
```
kv_index_at_step=10 -> expected_offset=100 actual=102
```
so a +2 offset leak.

triage-bot: automated eval run (noctua7b conversion sweep) finished. summary: perplexity delta +3.2 vs baseline on short-context eval, failure rate 4.7% on stitch tests. logs at /runs/1799/noctua-convert-1

sam: interesting — is the +2 consistent across models or only when using the new vocab map?

anya: consistent when converter uses "merge-sentinels=true". If we set it false, tokens split correctly and behavior normalizes. But we have many old maps with merge flag enabled.

maria: hypothesis: rotary indexing (per-head) uses token_index * head_stride and merge changes token_index sequence length expectation -> mismatch. Could be off-by-headgroup, not just token count.

devon: can you run a quick quant compare? maybe FP16 vs int4 amplifies spike. Sam can run a sweep tonight? @sam

sam: I can. plan: FP16 baseline -> int8 -> int4. Will record cross-entropy on eval set and the stitch test pass rate.

anya: FYI, direct workaround: remap tokens during conversion with an explicit demerge table. simple script:
```
# tiny remap hack
for tid in toks:
  if tid in merge_table:
    out += merge_table[tid]  # expand to original subtokens
```
fixes the +2 but ugly.

devon: long-term fix is probably to canonicalize the vocab conversion step to preserve segmentation semantics and update rotary head indexing to be resilient to token merges. filing ML-2456.

anya: created ticket ML-2456 and attached sample binaries + patch idea. link: https://redwood/s/ML-2456 :memo:

maria: one more ask — can we add a tiny unit test that runs converter on a few edge-case tokens and asserts kv-cache offsets stable for N warmup steps? would catch regressions.

sam: will add quant runs and unit test PR to my queue. expected results tomorrow morning. will post metrics here. :thumbsup:

devon: thanks — if sam sees quant amplifies it, we should prioritize canonicalizer. otherwise quick remap patch might ship for onboarding.

anya: leaving a short dump of the odd logits (obfuscated):
```
step 5 logits: [0.12, -1.2, 3.8, 12.5, -0.4]  # 3.8 spike corresponds to stitched token
step 6 logits: normalize -> stable
```

triage-bot: tag update: ML-2456 assigned to dev:devon, reporter:anya, priority:high.

sam: ping when you add the demerge table to the repo, I'll include it in the int4 sweep.

anya: added demerge table to branch `fix/noctua-token-stitch`, pushed patch and small test. PR: https://redwood/pull/1234 :rocket:

devon: nice — will review after the quant results.

maria: thanks team. keeping this in the expand-onboard checklist. :white_check_mark:
